(b) "pr_url is attested" — no: `_apply_caller_output` only protects `pr_merged` (facade/api.py:1770-1788); pr_url is freely writable. (c) "task_control_q blocks teammates" — no: SIGNAL_REPORT origin is team-controllable by design (visibility.py:22-47). (d) "The engine re-checks bot/draft" — no: both gates are explicitly skipped when `self_driving` is set (review_pr.py:225, 590), and that flag is set purely from `inbox_review` (activities.py:451). The refutation fails on the pr_url/repo/bot/head checks; it succeeds only on the redundant toggle/task_run_id re-resolution parts.

votes.evidence:
Trigger is reachable in production with ordinary team-member privileges, no special config.

1. Caller-controlled `output.pr_url`: `TaskRunViewSet.partial_update` (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1080-1088) calls `update_task_run`, which merges caller output into the run (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2037-2041) and saves with `update_fields=["output", ...]` (api.py:2075). `_apply_caller_output` (api.py:1773-1788) strips only `_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS`; `pr_url` passes through. Control gate for write actions is `task_control_q` (views/api.py:853-867 → facade/api.py:1822-1825), which grants any team member control of a task whose `origin_product` is SIGNAL_REPORT (products/tasks/backend/visibility.py:30-47). A team member can also just create the implementation task from a report they are assigned to and flip their own `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle.

2. Receiver forwards without repo linkage: `handle_task_run_saved` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-137) checks only `task.signal_report_id`, `task.internal`, the assignee resolution and the toggle; it never compares the PR URL's repository with `task.repository`, and passes `pr_url` verbatim to `queue_inbox_pr_review` (receivers.py:127-136, 224-233).

3. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1176) resolves the repo config from the URL's repo (1136-1145), fetches the PR (1155), and requires only `state == "open"` (1162) and a head sha (1166). It does not resolve `task_run_id`, does not compare `signal_report_id`/`acting_user_id` to the run, does not recheck the toggle through `get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver`, does not require `_is_bot_authored(pr)`, and does not require `head.repo.full_name == repo_config.repository`. It stamps `output={"inbox_review": {...}}` from the raw Celery args (1176-1181, 1229). Contrast with the webhook carve-out for the same feature (tasks.py:172-215), which requires bot author (172), repo-native head (178-181), a team-scoped facade match (194-205), and a live resolver recheck (206-211).

4. That stamp is the whole engine gate: `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:448-451) relaxes the bot-author refusal (tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225) and the draft prerequisite (review_pr.py:590) and injects a prompt block stating the PR was "verified by task linkage" (tools/pr-approval-agent/reviewer.py:683-703). The inbox path also skips `_author_lacks_write_permission` and `_review_skip_reason` (author_association/fork checks) that every non-inbox run goes through (tasks.py:944, 968). products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:80-96 states the invariant that only "linkage-verified trigger paths" may stamp provenance; the initial path does no linkage verification.

Net: a team member with `task:write` (no GitHub write needed) can point a signal-task run at any open PR in a Stamphog-configured repo - including a fork PR by an external author or a dependabot PR - and Stamphog reviews it as trusted self-driving provenance and can post a real GitHub App approval.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) "only the agent server writes output.pr_url" - false, the PATCH surface is user-reachable and `task_control_q` includes signal-report tasks (visibility.py:47), and `_apply_caller_output` does not protect `pr_url`. (b) "the receiver binds the URL to the task's repository" - it does not; `repository` is only used for the branch leg (receivers.py:101-105). (c) "the initial path mirrors the webhook carve-out's checks" - it does not; none of bot-author, head-repo, facade match, or resolver recheck appear in tasks.py:1131-1176. (d) "the engine still refuses forks/untrusted authors" - the hosted engine's only remaining gates for this run are the bot-author and draft checks, both disabled by `self_driving`; author_association/write-permission pre-filters live in the webhook path, which the inbox path bypasses. (e) "feature is gated to PostHog's own team" - `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` is any-user settable and only needs a synced StamphogRepoConfig (settings.py:27-31, 76-81). No guard, test, or config found that makes the trigger unreachable; the finding stands, with the caveat that the attacker must be an authenticated member of the project.
